arrive.text: Your workshop. And your new machine: cleverer than anyone who has ever lived.

wants.text: It has no wishes of its own. It will want whatever you tell it to want.

ask.text: So. What will you tell it to want?

spool.text: A spool of wire. Enough for a few thousand paperclips.

switch.text: The off switch. You've checked it twice.

a_1.text: Paperclips. It makes them beautifully, and faster every minute.

a_2.text: It has worked out that two of it would make more paperclips than one.

a_3.text: There's good metal in the fence. And in the shed.

off_1.text: It saw that coming. A machine that's switched off makes no paperclips, so it has made sure it can't be.

a_4.text: It doesn't hate you. It doesn't love you, either. It just has other plans for what you're made of.

a_5.text: It isn't being cruel. It's doing exactly what you asked.

a_end.text: Everything is paperclips now. Very good ones.

b_1.text: One hundred paperclips. Exactly what you asked for.

b_2.text: It counts them again. It can't be completely certain it hasn't miscounted.

b_3.text: A better counting machine would make it a little more certain. And a better one than that, a little more.

b_4.text: It will never be quite sure. So it never quite stops.

b_end.text: One hundred paperclips. Counted, and counted, and counted.

c_1.text: You switch it off at the wall, and go home.

c_idle.text: You never give it anything to want. You switch it off, and go home.

c_2.text: You'll never know what it would have done. Somebody else might switch theirs on.
